reports.title: Brian Mitchell: Prevention of Future Deaths Report

concerns.quote: In the two years that have elapsed since Brian's death investigations have been conducted by the British Transport Police, The Rail Accident Investigation Branch ("RAIB") and TFL into the circumstances that led to this incident. There is no clear evidence to demonstrate that risks of fatal harm have been mitigated.
Recommended technological measures to detect and alert staff to the presence of persons on the tracks have not been implemented at Stratford station.
concerns.hazard: absence of detection and alert technology

concerns.quote: No clear data is available to demonstrate that training provided to train operators (drivers) to ensure that they concentrate and look at the tracks before them whilst operating trains using ATO has resulted in positive improvement in performance.
concerns.hazard: lack of evidence of training effectiveness

concerns.quote: No clear data is available to demonstrate that station staff training has improved expedition or clarity of communication in emergency circumstances.
concerns.hazard: lack of evidence of staff training impact

links.explanation: Both reports concern the lack of effective detection of persons on or near railway tracks/platforms. The earlier report focuses on staff noticing odd behaviour and tracking via CCTV, while the later report calls for technological detection of people on the tracks.
